title: There’s a New, International Food Pyramid in Town - Nautilus
gist: A new international food pyramid based on dietary guidelines from around the world arrives as the U.S. guidance has swung from a carb-heavy 1992 pyramid to a 2011 plate to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s inverted pyramid. Kennedy's version prioritizes protein, dairy, fats, vegetables and fruit, minimizes whole grains, and declares a new war on sugar.

insights.claim: The original 1992 U.S. food pyramid recommended 6 to 11 daily servings of bread, cereals, rice, and pasta as its foundation.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Shifts in official guidance away from carbohydrates have long-run implications for grain-based food demand.
